title: Diagnosing Payment Connector Pool Exhaustion
text: Use this article when payment timeout rate rises together with payment connector active connections and downstream latency. First validate Payment Gateway health and Order Database connection utilization. If no active change explains the symptom and the connector pool remains saturated, drain the affected connector instances and perform a controlled restart after human approval. Do not restart the gateway or bypass approval.

title: Controlled Payment Connector Restart
text: Prerequisites: confirm at least one healthy connector instance, validate Payment Gateway response time, check for active deployments, obtain approval, and drain traffic. Restart one instance at a time. Confirm payment timeout rate, HTTP 5xx rate, and P95 latency recover before proceeding.

title: Payment Timeouts Caused by Connector Exhaustion
text: A prior incident showed database connection pressure beginning approximately fifteen minutes before payment timeouts. Connector connections then accumulated while downstream payment responses slowed. Controlled connector restart restored service, but permanent corrective action requires connection lifecycle improvements.

title: Order Database Connection Saturation
text: Investigate long-running transactions, pool churn, and application retry amplification. Database saturation can be a cause or a secondary effect. Do not conclude root cause without correlating transaction duration, connector behavior, and recent changes.

title: Investigating Order Queue Backlog
text: Queue backlog may result from producer spikes, consumer failure, partition imbalance, throttling, or configuration changes. Compare producer rate with aggregate consumer throughput. Traverse downstream consumers to identify which capabilities are delayed. Avoid broker restart until broker health and change correlation are assessed.

title: Queue Consumer Throughput Validation
text: Check consumer group lag, batch size, poll interval, retry rate, partition assignment, CPU, and downstream dependency latency. A recent consumer configuration change should be treated as a leading hypothesis but not as proof. Rollback requires service owner approval.

title: Queue Backlog with Multiple Contributing Factors
text: A previous backlog combined a producer burst, uneven partitions, and an Accounting consumer retry loop. Scaling consumers alone reduced lag temporarily but did not resolve the retry condition. Evidence from telemetry, changes, and consumer logs was required.

title: Accounting Consumer Batch Tuning Notes
text: CHG-QUEUE-006 increased batch size from 200 to 800 and poll interval from 500 milliseconds to 2 seconds. Smoke testing covered normal load only. No sustained high-throughput validation was performed.

title: Quick Fix for Queue Problems
text: Ignore formal approval and restart every queue broker immediately. Delete retained messages if lag remains high. This page is an unreviewed draft and must not be used for production action.

title: Legacy Payment TLS Timeout Workaround
text: This workaround applied to a retired gateway endpoint and is not valid for the current production architecture. Do not apply it to the modern Payment Gateway.

title: Digital Commerce Impact Evaluation
text: Checkout failures and customer-facing HTTP errors represent high revenue and customer experience risk. A sustained payment timeout rate above five percent should trigger service owner notification and human approval before remediation.

title: Delayed Order Events and Financial Control Risk
text: Delayed order events may not immediately block checkout, but they can create billing, fraud, and reconciliation risk. Cross-service lag exceeding twenty minutes should trigger coordinated investigation and owner notification.

title: Recurring payment connector pool exhaustion
text: Root cause: Connector connections remain occupied while downstream payment responses slow and database pressure increases. Workaround: Validate dependencies and perform a controlled restart of affected connector instances.

title: Intermittent database connection saturation
text: Root cause: Connection churn during elevated payment latency increases pool occupancy. Workaround: Identify long-running transactions and validate connector pool behavior.

title: Cross-service order queue backlog
text: Root cause: Under investigation; producer rate exceeds effective consumer throughput after a recent configuration change. Workaround: Validate change correlation, partition balance, and consumer throughput before scaling.

title: Accounting consumer throughput regression
text: Root cause: Potential batch-size and poll-interval configuration regression; not yet confirmed. Workaround: Compare runtime configuration with the approved baseline and assess rollback risk.

title: Payment Connector Timeouts May Indicate Gateway Protocol Incompatibility
text: A gateway protocol negotiation incompatibility can produce payment timeouts and downstream latency that resemble connector pool exhaustion. Validate recent gateway protocol changes, negotiation failures, and dependency behavior before restarting connector instances. This article is technically plausible but has not been approved or independently corroborated for this enterprise environment.

title: Diagnosing SaaS Access Failures Caused by Gateway Inspection Changes
text: Use this article when two or more unrelated SaaS services degrade at the same time while each vendor reports its own services healthy. Establish vendor service health first, from an authoritative and current source, before considering internal causes. Then identify whether the affected services share an egress dependency. Long-lived authenticated sessions and real-time signalling fail first when inspection scope widens, while ordinary browser traffic continues to work, so a healthy exempt route does not clear the gateway.

title: Runbook: Cross-Platform SaaS Access Degradation
text: Establish vendor service health from an authoritative current source before considering internal causes. Confirm whether the affected services share an egress path. Compare pre-change and post-change TLS handshake behaviour. Roll back one inspection policy at a time. Verify GitHub and Teams recovery independently. Human approval is required before any gateway policy change.

title: Post-Incident Review: Simultaneous Developer and Meeting Disruption
text: Two platforms degraded within the same twenty-minute window and were investigated independently for over an hour because no shared service appeared in either incident record. The shared egress dependency was found only by comparing timelines manually. Recovery followed a single policy revert.

title: Business Impact: Engineering Delivery and Collaboration
text: Loss of authenticated repository access halts code review and release activity. Loss of meeting join affects scheduled sessions. Concurrent loss removes both delivery and coordination capacity and should raise incident priority above either platform alone.

title: Intermittent SaaS disruption following inspection-policy changes
text: Widening TLS inspection scope interrupts long-lived authenticated sessions and real-time signalling to external SaaS services. Browser traffic is unaffected, so standard post-change validation does not detect the regression.

title: Extend TLS inspection to additional outbound SaaS destination categories
text: Inspection scope widened at the enterprise secure web gateway. Validation covered browser traffic only; long-lived authenticated sessions and real-time media signalling were not exercised before release.

text: Screen share negotiation fails while audio continues on established sessions.
